# Turn Any Meeting into a Clear AI Summary in Minutes

You’ve just walked out of a meeting full of ideas, decisions and deadlines, but your notebook looks more like a doodle pad than a record. Imagine if you could capture every point without the frantic scribbling, and get a tidy summary in a few minutes. That extra clarity can free up mental space for the real work that matters.

## Set up live transcription

The easiest way to turn spoken words into text is to enable live transcription during the call.

- **Choose a voice‑to‑text service** such as Otter.ai, Microsoft Copilot, or the built‑in transcription in Google Meet.  
- **Turn on live captions** in Zoom or Microsoft Teams – it’s a single toggle in the meeting settings.  
- **Place your microphone close to the speaker** and keep background noise low. A headset with a noise‑cancelling mic works wonders.

> **What is transcription?** It’s the process of converting spoken language into written text, much like a stenographer typing everything you say in real time.

## Capture the audio if you missed the live feed

Sometimes you’ll realise the meeting is over before you’ve enabled transcription. Don’t worry – you can still get a record.

- **Record with your phone** using a voice‑recorder app that offers an offline transcription feature.  
- **Ask a colleague (with permission)** to share their recording.  
- **Upload the file to an AI‑powered audio tool** such as Descript or Riverside.fm; they will produce a transcript from the audio file.

## Feed the transcript to an AI summariser

Once you have a text version, let an AI do the heavy lifting.

1. **Copy the whole transcript** from your transcription tool.  
2. **Paste it into a conversational AI** – ChatGPT, Claude, or Google Gemini are good options.  
3. **Enter a clear prompt (instruction)**, for example:

   ```
   Summarise this meeting transcript in bullet points. Include key decisions, action items with owners, and any deadlines. Keep the summary under 150 words.
   ```

> **What is a prompt?** It’s simply the instruction you give the AI, similar to typing a question into a search box.

The AI will generate a concise list of the most important points.

## Refine the output and share

AI‑generated summaries are usually spot‑on, but a quick human review ensures nothing is missed.

- **Check names and numbers** – AI can mis‑hear “Megan” as “Meghan” or swap dates.  
- **Add any omitted details** in your own wording, especially context that only you know.  
- **Format for easy consumption:** use bold headings for sections (Decisions, Actions) and bullet points for each item.

> **Why refine?** A short review catches occasional errors and adds your personal touch, making the summary trustworthy for anyone who reads it.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use the same workflow to capture family discussions, study group meetings, or community‑group minutes. You’ll have a reliable record without the hassle of hand‑written notes.  
- **At work or in a business:** Turn every team sync, client call, or project kickoff into a tidy recap that can be emailed to the whole crew. This saves hours of typing and reduces the “I missed that point” emails.  
- **If you’re just starting:** Pick one upcoming meeting, enable live transcription, and run the resulting text through an AI summariser. You’ll see the process in action and understand how much time it frees up.

## Wrap‑up

By turning on live transcription, recording when needed, and feeding the text into an AI summariser, you can replace frantic note‑taking with clear, shareable minutes. The AI does the legwork; a quick glance adds confidence. Try this method at your next meeting and reclaim the mental space for the ideas that really matter.
